items.creator: Sahil Bloom
items.why: Amit first took Bloom for a self-help tweeter, then noticed how many of his tweets he was bookmarking.

items.title: Salil Chowdhury's music for Anand
items.creator: Salil Chowdhury
items.why: It is his soundtrack for a permitted half-hour of luxuriating in melancholy. Hindi cinema plays to that mood beautifully, as long as you don't let it take over your life.

items.title: Salt, Fat, Acid, Heat
items.creator: Samin Nosrat
items.why: It teaches you to think in four elements, how they act and combine. That makes it a great way to cook organically and go with the flow without always geeking out.

items.title: Salvador Dali's later work
items.creator: Salvador Dali
items.why: His later work 'hit me really hard', with an assurance that blew Amit away.

items.title: Sam Altman on being a generalist
items.creator: Sam Altman
items.why: Altman argues you can be a specialist while it's a project, but the moment you become a company founder you must step back and think broadly.

items.title: Sam Altman on focus
items.creator: Sam Altman
items.why: 'Focus is a force multiplier on work': working on the right thing matters more than working many hours, and Altman has yet to meet a slow-moving person who is very successful.

items.title: San Fransicko
items.creator: Michael Shellenberger
items.why: Amit calls it a great book. Among other factors, it shows how well-meant controls on prices helped make the city unaffordable.

items.title: Sarbpreet Singh Finds His Sikhism (The Seen and the Unseen, Ep 407)
items.creator: Amit Varma
items.why: A chance to hear at length from the historian behind the Khalsa Bridge story.

items.title: Sarkari Khatiya Private Karo
items.why: It is the comic set-piece that opens the episode.

items.title: Saumya Roy's book on the trash mountains of Bombay
items.creator: Saumya Roy
items.why: Ajay calls it amazing. It shows how badly Bombay handles its waste, which is why he avoids plastic.

items.title: Science Policy Resolution of 1958
items.why: Ajay calls it 'stirring' and 'goosebumps material': a dream of building India on rationalism, beyond superstition, with science as a way of life. Its dream remains worth honouring even if the 1947-era methods need rethinking.

items.title: Scrivener
items.why: The tool for writing books, another of the single-purpose apps Amit has used.

items.title: Secret Garden
items.creator: Bruce Springsteen
items.why: It seems carnal at first, then turns into a song about how you can never truly know another person and the recesses in each of us no one else can reach.

items.title: Seeing dead fruit flies is bad for the health of fruit flies
items.creator: Christi Gendron
items.why: The study showing that even fruit flies suffer shorter lives after seeing dead fruit flies, evidence that the mind 'goes all the way down to flies'.

items.title: Seizing the Enigma
items.creator: David Kahn
items.why: Its first two pages gripped him so completely that he skipped his commute and read the whole book in an Irani cafe until 9 pm.

items.title: Self Portrait Facing Death
items.creator: Pablo Picasso
items.why: Amit finds it 'genius' and 'masterful', proof that Picasso's late work deserved more respect than the critics of the time gave it.

items.title: Self-Portrait
items.creator: A.K. Ramanujan
items.why: A tiny poem on the same theme: the speaker resembles 'everyone but myself' and sees in shop windows the portrait of a stranger, 'often signed in a corner by my father'.

items.title: Seven Bridges Road
items.creator: Steve Young (original, 1969); The Eagles (live version, 1980)
items.why: He thinks both versions are wonderful. Amit reveals Ajay has sung his own cover.

items.title: Seven Pillars of Wisdom
items.creator: T. E. Lawrence
items.why: It is part of the early literature on guerrilla war that existed long before the US went into Vietnam and still failed to learn from it.

items.title: Sexual Behavior in the Human Female
items.creator: Alfred Kinsey and others
items.why: It showed that women have rich sexual lives (masturbation, fantasy, partners beyond their husbands), overturning the belief that sexuality was mainly a male thing.

items.title: Sexual Behavior in the Human Male
items.creator: Alfred Kinsey and others
items.why: It blew apart myths of its time, for instance showing that about a third of men admitted a homosexual experience. Amit notes its limits: an elite Western sample and self-reported preferences.

items.title: Shahab Bakhtiari's quote tweet extending Milanfar's rule
items.creator: Shahab Bakhtiari
items.why: An argument for reading across disciplines and places. It ties to Ajay's complaint about American economists generalising from a study of Arizona to the whole world.

items.title: Shallow
items.creator: Lady Gaga and Bradley Cooper
items.why: One of the only recent songs Ajay knows and loves.

items.title: Shane Parrish's books
items.creator: Shane Parrish
items.why: 'Shane Parrish's books are great.' A good source for building a toolkit of mental models.

items.title: Shane Parrish's tweet on working from home
items.creator: Shane Parrish
items.why: Its gist is that people who show up at the office will end up as bosses of those who work from home. Amit's reading is not about bureaucratic presence: real creativity happens in water-cooler talk and after-work beers.

items.title: Short Cuts
items.creator: Robert Altman
items.why: Amit was excited because its structure echoed Altman's Nashville. He admits he was a little disappointed, perhaps because of anchoring, since he was comparing it with Nashville and with Carver's original stories.

items.title: Shruti Jahagirdar (nutritionist and physical trainer)
items.why: She designs a complete plan around your body weight and goals, advises vegetarians on keto, and believes in resistance training. She also taught Amit to skip multivitamins and take specific supplements such as B12, E and C.

items.title: Shruti Jahagirdar is the Sporty One (The Seen and the Unseen, Ep 289)
items.creator: Amit Varma with Shruti Jahagirdar
items.why: A way to get to know her approach before consulting her.

items.title: Shruti Rajagopalan Remembers the Angle of the Light (The Seen and the Unseen, Ep 410)
items.creator: Amit Varma
items.why: It's 'precisely on this subject': she's a disruptor in how capital is allocated.

items.title: Sign of the Times
items.creator: Harry Styles
items.why: A song he genuinely loves, and Harry Styles is called 'bloody good'. A reason not to look down on new music.

items.title: Signull's newsletter
items.creator: Signull
items.why: The quality of the content, which he finds genuinely thought-provoking.

items.title: Simon Sinek on Nike's mission
items.creator: Simon Sinek
items.why: It shows a brand built on 'we are with you when you do', not on selling shoes. Amit says it moves him.

items.title: Simulating Pension Income Scenarios with penCalc
items.creator: Renuka Sane and William Price
items.why: An example of the pension income simulation work Ajay says India badly needs more of.

items.title: Sinocism
items.creator: Bill Bishop
items.why: Bishop isn't a mainstream name, and he writes about China in a way so specialised that mainstream outlets might never commission him. Yet he is a superstar among his subscribers.

items.title: Sirf Ek Naam Sunayi Deta Hai (Chak De India)
items.why: The state-team captain versus national coach clash anticipates the shift from local satraps to one national firm.

items.title: Six Degrees
items.creator: Duncan Watts
items.why: It explains how connected the world is, which is the science behind Ajay's model of transmission loss in human networks.

items.title: Six More Stories That Should Be Films (Everything is Everything, Ep 43)
items.creator: Amit Varma and Ajay Shah
items.why: More film pitches in the same format.

items.title: Sleepify
items.creator: Vulfpeck
items.why: An album of 30-second tracks meant to loop all night while fans slept, and it made the band money until Spotify caught on.

items.title: Slouching Towards Utopia
items.creator: Bradford De Long
items.why: It gives a better structural understanding of the old economic policy consensus that existed before Trump, Putin, Xi Jinping and the right-wing authoritarians.

items.title: Slow Productivity
items.creator: Cal Newport
items.why: It argues you don't need a constant mad sprint. You can live a quiet life and let ideas marinate, and creativity emerges from that over time. A counterweight to hustle culture.

items.title: Smoke And Mirrors
items.creator: Pallavi Aiyar
items.why: Amit calls Aiyar a fantastic writer and a sharp analyst, not just a travel writer. The book gives a ground-level view of China's transformation and how people absorbed it.

items.title: Snatching decline from the jaws of growth
items.creator: KP Krishnan
items.why: It proposes a practical wedge: fully deregulate labour law in IT and IT-enabled services, where workers obviously don't need paternalistic protection, then expand to other industries if it works.

items.title: Social conformity despite individual preferences for distinctiveness
items.creator: Paul Smaldino and Joshua Epstein
items.why: The title captures what happens on campus. Young people arrive convinced they are independent rebels and end up conforming to the fashion of the day anyway.

items.title: Socialism: An Economic and Sociological Analysis
items.creator: Ludwig von Mises
items.why: This is the book that turned the young Hayek from democratic socialism and Marxism into a classical liberal.

items.title: Solitude
items.why: Spend time with yourself and think about life. Watch yourself approach a problem 'just like a cat approaches a prey'.

items.title: Solving the intermittency of renewables
items.creator: Akshay Jaitly and Ajay Shah
items.why: Deeper reading on the episode's central puzzle: how to cope when solar disappears exactly as evening demand surges.

items.title: Son of Bosey
items.creator: Anand Ramachandran
items.why: The great blog of Anand Ramachandran, whom Amit calls perhaps the funniest man in Indian history.

items.title: Song of Myself, 51
items.creator: Walt Whitman
items.why: The source of 'we contain multitudes', Amit's excuse for offering advice that contradicts itself.

items.title: Sonnet 18
items.creator: William Shakespeare
items.why: Shakespeare was never wrapped in cotton wool, so everyone has reworked him, which is how culture should work.

items.title: Sonnet 18 (Akala performance)
items.creator: Akala
items.why: Shows Shakespeare turned into hip hop. Amit says culture is a party: mix karo, dance karo, enjoy karo.

items.title: Sonnet 18 (David Gilmour performance)
items.creator: David Gilmour
items.why: An example of a classic being freely remixed across eras and genres.

items.title: South vs North
items.creator: Nilakantan RS
items.why: It supplies striking comparisons: life expectancy of 75 in Kerala versus 64 in UP, and infant mortality of 7 in Kerala versus 48 in Madhya Pradesh. It also shows that Kerala battles diabetes and obesity while the heartland battles malnutrition and stunting.

items.title: Stack is the New Black?
items.creator: Smriti Parsheera
items.why: A critical look at the 'India Stack' approach to digital infrastructure.

items.title: Stalemate, Zugzwang and a long Middle Game
items.creator: Lawrence Freedman
items.why: Freedman's take on whether the war is a stalemate, in the same chess-flavoured terms the hosts use.

items.title: State-of-the-art reviews of the Indian bankruptcy reform (2016, 2017, 2018)
items.creator: The Leap Journal blog
items.why: Year-by-year snapshots of how the reform was progressing: the kind of ongoing public criticism Ajay says keeps policymakers honest.

items.title: Statistical Basis for Predicting Technological Progress
items.creator: Béla Nagy, J Doyne Farmer, Quan M Bui and Jessika E Trancik
items.why: He calls it a beautiful paper and mind-blowing data work. It assembled productivity curves for 62 industries, tested rival laws of progress, and found Wright's Law (aggregate lifetime volume) the best predictor.

items.title: Steve Jobs hates consultants
items.creator: Steve Jobs
items.why: Jobs's rule was to hire the best people and ignore consultants, who have no skin in the game.

items.title: Steve Jobs on hiring
items.creator: Steve Jobs
items.why: Everything depends on your first five hires. A-list people attract other A-list people, and that becomes the culture.

items.title: Stocks for the Long Run
items.creator: Jeremy Siegel
items.why: It builds the basic intuition from two hundred years of equity index investing, which is the foundation of the episode's whole argument. He says everybody should read it and take the message in deeply.

items.title: Strategy: A History
items.creator: Lawrence Freedman
items.why: Amit calls it masterful and magisterial, a book packed with knowledge and insight that he learned a lot from.

items.title: Studies on dating trends (Pew 2023, SoulMatcher 2025, OkCupid 2017, GDI 2025, Tinder 2025, IJCHP 2024)
items.why: Sources for the findings on age preferences, swipe rates and the Tinder Gini coefficient.

items.title: Sun of the Family
items.why: The producers interviewed his parents, brother and girlfriend, and a whole person comes alive through the inflections in their voices and their particular memories. Amit calls it heartbreaking and a second landmark of show, don't tell.

items.title: Supernova in the East
items.creator: Dan Carlin
items.why: It is the source of the story of the soldier who defended a Philippine island for 29 years because nobody told him the war was over.

items.title: Surface Area of Luck
items.creator: Model Thinkers
items.why: It gives the episode's central formula: your chance of being lucky equals the action you take on your passion multiplied by the number of people you effectively tell about it.

items.title: Susan Thomas's book club in Bombay
items.creator: Susan Thomas
items.why: An in-person reading community in Bombay. Joining one is the ultimate way to design your environment for reading.

items.title: Suzanne
items.creator: Leonard Cohen
items.why: A 'really, really deep song' and 'one of the great songs to know'.

items.title: Swachh Bharat (The Seen and the Unseen, Ep 82)
items.creator: Amit Varma with Shruti Rajagopalan
items.why: Shows how a well-intentioned scheme that ignored its supporting infrastructure ended up reinforcing caste practices.

items.title: Sweetness and Power
items.creator: Sidney Mintz
items.why: It provides the historical grounding for understanding sugar's hold on us.

items.title: Taking the Hands
items.creator: Robert Bly
items.why: It is a great poem, and it shows how a whole universe can fit into something small, which sets up an episode about maps.

items.title: Talking Heads (YouTube channel)
items.creator: Talking Heads
items.why: The band that made Byrne, and Byrne's ideas about music, matter to him.

items.title: Talking to an Empty Room
items.creator: Sharad Joshi
items.why: The title breaks Amit's heart. Joshi spent years in Parliament with great ideas that nobody paid attention to, and the country would have gained a lot by listening.

items.title: Tan on co-CEOs
items.creator: Garry Tan
items.why: Co-CEOs may suit the founders but slow every decision for everyone below them. Have one decision-maker.

items.title: Tangerine
items.creator: Led Zeppelin
items.why: Years ago he came across the lyrics before hearing it and wondered what kind of song they would make. The actual song is surprising and brilliant, and 'it'll just make you think about songs.'

items.title: Taxes Should Be Used for Governance, Not Politics
items.creator: Amit Varma
items.why: It continues the episode's argument that because taxes are taken by force, how they are spent has to be justified.

items.title: TB Sheets
items.creator: Van Morrison
items.why: Another great long song, by Van Morrison, a hero to both Springsteen and Amit.

items.title: Technology, Taxation, and Corruption: Evidence from the Introduction of Electronic Tax Filing
items.creator: Oyebola Okunogbe and Victor Pouliquen
items.why: A cautionary example rather than an endorsement. Ajay argues that outcomes credited to e-filing actually come from hundreds of surrounding details of law, administration, culture and norms.

items.title: Television Price Controls (The Seen and the Unseen, Ep 27)
items.creator: Amit Varma
items.why: Ashok Malik explains why Indian TV news is so bad: government price caps on subscriptions forced channels to depend on advertising and race to the bottom.

items.title: Terror as a Bargaining Instrument: A Case Study of Dowry Violence in Rural India
items.creator: Francis Bloch and Vijayendra Rao
items.why: The research found domestic violence was often a rational strategy to extract money from the wife's family, which pushed economists to rethink how they model household and transfer behaviour.

items.title: Testaments Betrayed
items.creator: Milan Kundera
items.why: Amit loves Kundera's image of a man in a fog who makes his road step by step; looking back, observers see the road but not the fog.

items.title: TeX
items.creator: Donald Knuth
items.why: A professional typesetting system used for many great books. Its author considers it finished and it has no recorded bugs, a rare level of craftsmanship in software.

items.title: The 2000 Business World article on Sonictown
items.creator: Business World
items.why: The surviving trace of a venture that otherwise left no mark on the internet.

items.title: The age of the partial outsider
items.creator: Janan Ganesh
items.why: It names a useful stance: being close enough to a field to have influence but outside enough not to be bound by its conventions.

items.title: The Alchemy of Finance
items.creator: George Soros
items.why: Source of the concept that the narratives imposed on a system change how that system sees and shapes itself.

items.title: The ancient fabric that no one knows how to make
items.creator: Zaria Gorvett
items.why: Amit says Gorvett has written many other excellent pieces on similar subjects that are worth checking out.

items.title: The Answer is 42
items.creator: Amit Varma
items.why: Part of the set of columns he points readers to for depth beyond the presentation.

items.title: The Art of Narrative Nonfiction (The Seen and the Unseen, Ep 183)
items.creator: Amit Varma with Samanth Subramanian
items.why: The longer conversation behind the Haldane stories and the 'show, don't tell' example.

items.title: The Art of Reading (Everything is Everything, Ep 120)
items.creator: Amit Varma and Ajay Shah
items.why: Both hosts love books, and the episode covers why and how to read better.

items.title: The Ascent of Man (TV series)
items.creator: Jacob Bronowski
items.why: A sweeping history of scientific thought that has shaped Ajay since childhood and is full of stories like these.

items.title: The Aser Reports
items.creator: Aser Centre
items.why: Simple measurement of learning done at scale every year. Ajay calls it the glory of the field and a milestone in Indian education.

items.title: The Atheism Episode (Everything is Everything, Ep 83)
items.creator: Amit Varma and Ajay Shah
items.why: 'Awesome episode, I'm very proud of it.'

items.title: The Balancing Act
items.creator: Amit Varma
items.why: Part of the set of columns he points readers to for depth beyond the presentation.

items.title: The Ballad of John Axon
items.why: A landmark in audio history. Interviews and background sound recorded in Axon's village went into the final piece, making it a masterclass in show, don't tell.

items.title: The Battle of Kursk
items.why: Russia's defences today come straight from that Soviet playbook, and Ukraine has so far cut through only one to one-and-a-half of three or four lines.

items.title: The Battle of the Atlantic
items.why: He thinks it is underrated and one of the most interesting stories of the Second World War, about how ingenuity, effort, imagination and creativity together won the battle for the Allies.

items.title: The Bear Came Over the Mountain
items.creator: Alice Munro
items.why: It is perhaps Amit's favourite short story of all time, and he calls it 'just magnificent'.

items.title: The Beautiful Tree
items.creator: James Tooley
items.why: A 'wonderful book' on budget private schools serving the poor, grounded in work among poor families and how they actually choose. 'Do read that as well.'

items.title: The Big Fat Surprise
items.creator: Nina Teicholz
items.why: It shows how the low-fat dogma and the Ancel Keys era misled a generation, and how dissenters were silenced.

items.title: The BIGGEST Day of My Career (Chris Horner on his Vuelta a España win)
items.creator: Chris Horner
items.why: A first-hand account of how the oldest Grand Tour winner pulled it off.

items.title: The BIS list of sanctions
items.creator: Bureau of Industry and Security
items.why: Anyone in business should know who is on the list. Dealing with a listed entity can land you in trouble, and being listed (about 12 Indian entities are) cuts you off from US travel, finance and trade.

items.title: The BJP Before Modi (The Seen and the Unseen, Ep 202)
items.creator: Amit Varma
items.why: Source of Sitapati's line 'Never let perfection be the enemy of production'.

items.title: The Black Paintings (especially The Dog)
items.creator: Francisco Goya
items.why: Amit calls the half hour he spent there an emotionally moving experience and went back for more. The Dog, untitled and unexplained, gives a sense of profound desolation.

items.title: The Blue Book, The Yellow Book and The Green Book
items.creator: Amitava Kumar
items.why: The books are journals combining writing and drawing, and they model the daily writing habit Amit says will shape you into a richer, deeper person.

items.title: The Book Club: Frankenstein (Storytel audio episode)
items.creator: Amit Varma
items.why: A fifteen-minute audio take on Frankenstein, to pair with the Wollstonecraft episode.

items.title: The Book of Love
items.creator: Magnetic Fields
items.why: Its idea of something old and mysterious leads into how mysterious the world once was before maps. Ajay adds that love is still a mystery, but our understanding of space has been transformed.

items.title: The Book That Incited a Worldwide Fear of Overpopulation
items.creator: Charles Mann
items.why: It shows the global scale of the coercion: health workers paid per IUD inserted, birth-control pills pitched out of helicopters over villages in the Philippines, and millions sterilised, often coercively, from Mexico to Bangladesh.

items.title: The books of Albert O. Hirschman
items.creator: Albert O. Hirschman
items.why: Hirschman wasn't wrong about linkages; they simply moved beyond national borders. Thinkers aren't obliged to be precisely correct fifty years later, and Ajay calls him 'one of the great people' whose books and biography everyone should read.

items.title: The bookshop ritual: buying each other books
items.why: An easy ritual to start with friends that introduces each of you to books you would never have picked yourself.

items.title: The Botany of Desire
items.creator: Michael Pollan
items.why: It captures, better than any statistic, how intoxicating and addictive sugar is from the very first taste.

items.title: The Bridge: The Life and Rise of Barack Obama
items.creator: David Remnick
items.why: Full of revealing detail, including the trivia that Obama played poker to network with Democratic Party insiders.

items.title: The Cambridge Economic History of Modern South Asia
items.creator: Edited by Latika Chaudhary, Tirthankar Roy and Anand Swamy
items.why: He has seen the table of contents and calls it 'drool'. The best people have been brought together, and he expects a gorgeous book.

items.title: The Case Against Education
items.creator: Bryan Caplan
items.why: It matches the episode's argument. Amit thinks the whole paradigm of schooling is broken: a system designed in the early 19th century to produce industrial workers, with same-age kids studying the same subjects. He sees a huge opportunity for whoever replaces it.

items.title: The Case Against Sugar
items.creator: Gary Taubes
items.why: In Amit's view it gives the best overarching account of the subject. It argues that sugar causes diabetes and obesity in the same causal sense that smoking causes lung cancer, through its hormonal effects rather than overeating. It is also the source of the Camel-cigarette history.

items.title: The Case for Flexible Exchange Rates (in Essays in Positive Economics)
items.creator: Milton Friedman
items.why: Friedman worked all of this out back in 1953. Ajay wants listeners to read it and admire the person who figured it out first.

items.title: The Categorical Imperative
items.creator: Immanuel Kant
items.why: He finds the formulation 'treat people as ends in themselves, not as means to an end' incredibly deep and beautiful. He says it enriches how we engage with others and has nothing to do with religion.

items.title: The Cats
items.creator: Ann Iverson
items.why: It is a delightful portrait of creatures who find glory in a dehydrated pea and find themselves 'so remarkable all the day long'. Ajay called it an aspirational statement; Amit called cats sociopaths.

items.title: The Citizenship Battles (The Seen and the Unseen, Ep 152)
items.creator: Amit Varma with Srinath Raghavan
items.why: He calls it a great episode on the CAA.

items.title: The Climb
items.creator: Chris Froome
items.why: Amit says it is great. It is a rider's-eye view from the Team Sky era discussed in the episode.

items.title: The collateral damage of regulatory roulette
items.creator: Vivek Ananth
items.why: Further reading on how unpredictable regulation causes damage, connected to Ajay's point that regulation is the core flaw.

items.title: The Collected Letters of Mary Wollstonecraft
items.creator: Mary Wollstonecraft
items.why: Amit calls it 'a beautiful book': Wollstonecraft's inner life in her own words.

items.title: The Collected Stories of Lydia Davis
items.creator: Lydia Davis
items.why: Fiction lets you enter the minds of others and live their lives. Davis is 'one of the great modern writers', and many of her stories are a paragraph or less. Literature keeps you learning without feeling like you are in learning mode.

items.title: The Collected Stories of Raymond Carver
items.creator: Raymond Carver
items.why: He ranks Carver among the great short-story writers: minimal, easy and elegant, in some ways a successor to Ernest Hemingway.

items.title: The Columbian Exchange
items.creator: Wikipedia
items.why: The background to why so much of 'Indian' food is actually from the Americas.

items.title: The Count of Monte Cristo
items.creator: Alexandre Dumas
items.why: It has a character named after Abbé Faria, which links the episode's mantra to classic literature.

items.title: The Creative Act
items.creator: Rick Rubin
items.why: Amit recommends it to all businessmen. Succeeding at anything takes imagination and thinking like a creator, so the book holds lessons for anyone starting a firm.

items.title: The Curious Incident of the Dog in the Night-time
items.creator: Mark Haddon
items.why: It shows what fiction can do: let you live inside a very different mind. Amit read out Haddon's own description: 'it's a novel about difference, about being an outsider, about seeing the world in a surprising and revealing way. It's as much a novel about us as it is about Christopher.'

items.title: The Dark Game
items.creator: Amit Varma
items.why: Amit has seen gambling addiction destroy lives up close; his columns deal with that dark side honestly, without asking for bans.

items.title: The Day Ryan Started Masturbating
items.creator: Amit Varma
items.why: It is the full telling of the episode's funniest illustration of mistaking sequence for causation.

items.title: The Diabetes Code
items.creator: Jason Fung
items.why: It lays out how type 2 diabetes can be reversed through diet, which is the premise of the whole episode.

items.title: The dialect of a cricket writer
items.creator: Amit Varma
items.why: His own catalogue of how sportswriting runs on stock phrases: human autocomplete in action.

items.title: The Disciple
items.creator: Chaitanya Tamhane
items.why: Its scene where a purist guru tells a student he can join a fusion band but must stop coming to class captures the idea that what you do determines who you become. Amit calls it good world cinema.

items.title: The Doctors' Plague
items.creator: Sherwin Nuland
items.why: The full story of Semmelweis: the discovery, the rejection and the tragic end.

items.title: The Dream Becomes a Reality
items.creator: Sagar Shah
items.why: Gukesh explains how he plays an unusual but not bad move order so that opponents must start thinking for themselves and wonder whether he has secret prep. It is a window into how elite players take rivals out of their preparation.

items.title: The Economic Legacies of Colonial Rule in India
items.creator: Tirthankar Roy
items.why: A 'fabulous essay' arguing the colonial economy was open to trade, capital and migration. It says economic nationalists misread payments to the British as a 'drain' when they were the price of tapping global markets for skills and capital.

items.title: The Economics of Child Labor
items.creator: Kaushik Basu and Pham Hoang Van
items.why: Calls it a great study. It helps work out the family income level at which children stop being sent to work, showing that growth is the long-term solution.

items.title: The Economics of Voting
items.creator: Amit Varma
items.why: Further reading on the voting questions discussed in the episode, such as rational ignorance and why people vote at all.

items.title: The Effect of Age-Specific Sex Ratios on Crime: Instrumental Variable Estimates from India
items.creator: Rashmi Barua, Prarthna Goel and Renuka Sane
items.why: Using an interesting identification strategy, it finds that when the sex ratio tilts toward excess males, crime rises.

items.title: The Elements of Programming Style
items.creator: Brian Kernighan and PJ Plauger
items.why: It carries the values of good prose into code: simplicity, elegance, being easy to understand, and not a word out of place.

items.title: The End of Faith
items.creator: Sam Harris
items.why: One of the founding New Atheist books whose critiques of organised religion Amit says you have to take seriously.

items.title: The End of History and the Last Man
items.creator: Francis Fukuyama
items.why: A rare case where the book is genuinely great and goes well beyond the essay it grew from.

items.title: The enduring legacy of Leo Szilard
items.creator: Ashutosh Jogalekar
items.why: Background on the physicist whose chain-reaction insight while crossing a London road set the bomb project in motion.

items.title: The Equity Premium: A Puzzle
items.creator: Rajnish Mehra and Edward Prescott
items.why: Ajay calls it an 'amazing paper', co-written by a friend of the show with one of the authors of the episode's key paper.

items.title: The Essential Dykes To Watch Out For
items.creator: Alison Bechdel
items.why: The comic strip ran for roughly 1985 to 2008 and became iconic. It captured, and arguably helped create, a lesbian counterculture. Its strip 'The Rule' gave the world the Bechdel test. It is also a model of steady, week-after-week craft.

items.title: The Euthyphro Dilemma
items.creator: Plato
items.why: It shows that even if God exists, morality cannot simply come from divine command.

items.title: The Evil of Family Planning
items.creator: Amit Varma
items.why: His earlier case that sterilisation camps and incentives still operate in India today, long after the Emergency.

items.title: The Evolution of Desire
items.creator: David Buss
items.why: It builds the evolutionary account of why men and women want what they want, which forms the shared ground this episode starts from.

items.title: The Evolution of Virulence
items.creator: Paul Ewald
items.why: It blew his mind. The idea that how easily a pathogen spreads determines how deadly it evolves to be is a lens you can't unsee.

items.title: The Experience Machine
items.creator: Robert Nozick
items.why: Nozick is one of Amit's favourite thinkers, but here Amit disagrees with him. The thought experiment is the clearest way into the question of whether machine-made feelings are worth less than real ones.

items.title: The Extended Case Method
items.creator: Michael Burawoy
items.why: It contrasts the positivist approach (detachment, standardised data, representative samples) with the reflexive one (engagement, embedding yourself in a community). Burawoy treats them as separate; Rao argues they can be combined.

items.title: The Fable of the Monkey and the Two Cats
items.creator: Pranay Kotasthane
items.why: Amit calls it a 'great newsletter post'. It shows why the vertical question (how much the centre passes down) matters more than states squabbling over their shares.

items.title: The Facebook study on Cross-Gender Social Ties
items.why: Ajay is excited because the data goes down to the smallest administrative units. He thinks researchers should use it as a standard measure of how separated men and women are in Indian cities and districts.

items.title: The Financial Expert
items.creator: RK Narayan
items.why: Ajay read it as a child, and it was where he first began thinking about a run on a bank.

items.title: The First Amendment to the US Constitution
items.why: 'Congress shall make no law... abridging the freedom of speech' has no caveats. US courts have interpreted it to protect all speech, hate speech included, short of direct incitement to violence, which is exactly where Amit draws his line.

items.title: The first PISA results for India: The end of the beginning
items.creator: Lant Pritchett
items.why: Pritchett on what India's first PISA results revealed.

items.title: The Forces That Shaped Hinduism (The Seen and the Unseen, Ep 405)
items.creator: Amit Varma with Manu Pillai
items.why: The fuller version of this story, especially on Savarkar. 'You should listen to that.'

items.title: The Friendship That Made Google Huge
items.creator: James Somers
items.why: Further reading on the engineering culture that, in Ajay's telling, let Google handle the world's largest computing problems.

items.title: The Future of War (Everything is Everything, Ep 112)
items.creator: Amit Varma and Ajay Shah
items.why: It sets out how modern war has changed, including long-range standoff weapons. That framing explains why Russian regions far from the Ukrainian border are being damaged.

items.title: The Game
items.creator: Neil Strauss
items.why: It is a manipulative pickup-artist handbook but shows a real understanding of human nature, and helps explain where today's manosphere came from.

items.title: The Garden Party and Other Plays
items.creator: Václav Havel
items.why: He says they are hilarious, available in English and worth reading in full. The plays dramatise Havel's conviction that language shapes reality.

items.title: The Gate of Angels
items.creator: Penelope Fitzgerald
items.why: It is proof that great fiction can come very late in life.

items.title: The Generation of Rage in Kashmir
items.creator: David Devadas
items.why: Devadas argues that 2007 was a moment of hope, with a new generation that wanted jobs and normal lives. He documents in detail how perverse incentives such as body-count rewards, rent-seeking and extortion wasted that moment and alienated people.

items.title: The Gentle Wisdom of Pratap Bhanu Mehta (The Seen and the Unseen, Ep 300)
items.creator: Amit Varma with Pratap Bhanu Mehta
items.why: It gives the opposing view to JP's: Pratap Bhanu Mehta believes PR would be an absolute disaster for India.

items.title: The Geopolitics of the Bangladesh War (The Seen and the Unseen, Ep 113)
items.creator: Amit Varma with Srinath Raghavan
items.why: Amit says the episode has been a 'gateway drug' for many listeners, and it gives the diplomatic background to 1971.

items.title: The German Tank Problem explained
items.creator: NStatum
items.why: A visual walk-through of the estimation idea Ajay describes, in which serial numbers reveal how many tanks were made.

items.title: The Girl From Haryana
items.creator: Amit Varma
items.why: It is the fuller account of how a historical accident created the Haryana women's wrestling cluster.

items.title: The Godfather
items.creator: Mario Puzo
items.why: It is a story about a family enterprise. Amit calls the book 'bloody good' and counts it, along with the films, among the masterpieces.

items.title: The Godfather
items.creator: Francis Ford Coppola
items.why: A masterpiece about a family enterprise, and Coppola at his absolute peak.

items.title: The Godfather Part II
items.creator: Francis Ford Coppola
items.why: Amit says both films are masterpieces and that together they are Coppola at his peak.

items.title: The Good Gyan Episode (Everything is Everything, Ep 93)
items.creator: Amit Varma and Ajay Shah
items.why: More wisdom gathered from social media in the same format.

items.title: The Good Lion
items.creator: Ernest Hemingway
items.why: A Hemingway story Amit loves, about a lion who badly wants a Hindu trader sandwich. He calls it 'a lovely formulation'.

items.title: The GPT 5 Deep Research Info Dump on Financial Crises
items.creator: ChatGPT
items.why: He thought it 'pretty good' for historical background and for summarising how Austrians, Keynesians and monetarists, as well as Minsky and Bernanke individually, read each crisis. It helps readers think for themselves.

items.title: The Great Arc
items.creator: John Keay
items.why: It tells the story of the early Survey of India and the first mapping of the country. In his words, it is 'a heroic tale' and 'so much fun.'

items.title: The Great Breakthrough and Its Cause
items.creator: Julian Simon
items.why: It extends Simon's argument that the industrial revolution and productivity booms happened because population rose. More people multiply the opportunities for free trade and voluntary exchange, and everyone benefits.

items.title: The Great Illusion
items.creator: Norman Angell
items.why: Worth knowing as a cautionary tale. Trade's incentives are real, but treating them as a guarantee is a mistake.

items.title: The Great Mental Models (three-volume set)
items.creator: Shane Parrish (Farnam Street)
items.why: Formal education rarely teaches how to think about the world. These books supply the frames for finding connections across fields, which is the 'everything is everything' idea in practice. Amit calls them a treasure everyone should own, and notes the Kindle copies are cheap.

items.title: The hard lessons from Ukraine's summer offensive
items.creator: Christopher Miller and Ben Hall (Financial Times)
items.why: It vividly describes the counteroffensive as 'a war of tree lines': small infantry groups advancing field by field under artillery and drones, slowly wearing down Russian defences.

items.title: The Hedgehog and the Fox
items.creator: Isaiah Berlin
items.why: It frames Oppenheimer as someone with fox-like range, from Sanskrit to philosophy, who was also an expert in several fields.

items.title: The Hidden Life of Trees
items.creator: Peter Wohlleben
items.why: It shows that a natural forest is a communicating system, with roots talking to each other and trees adjusting when one is harmed. It made Amit see that planting forty trees together is not an ecosystem, and it challenges the human belief that we have figured everything out.

items.title: The Hindi Heartland
items.creator: Ghazala Wahab
items.why: Has a 'great excerpt' on tribals made to tick a 'Hindu' box, and the mass movement now reasserting their earlier identities.

items.title: The History and Geography of Human Genes
items.creator: Luca Cavalli-Sforza
items.why: Showed that genetic evidence can reveal, with surprising certainty, when people arrived somewhere and who they mixed with.

items.title: The History of the Planning Commission (The Seen and the Unseen, Ep 306)
items.creator: Amit Varma
items.why: It goes into detail on the Mahalanobis period and the planning mindset that held that competition is wasteful.

items.title: The Hobbit
items.creator: J.R.R. Tolkien
items.why: Another case of a person writing to family and ending up with a book the world treasures.

items.title: The Hollow Man
items.creator: John Dickson Carr
items.why: A 1935 crime novel voted the greatest locked-room murder mystery of all time. It walks through the solutions to other locked-room mysteries, including the classic melting ice cube.

items.title: The Honest Broker
items.creator: Ted Gioia
items.why: Amit calls Gioia a deep meta-thinker about music and the music business.

items.title: The Idea Factory: Bell Labs and the Great Age of American Innovation
items.creator: Jon Gertner
items.why: It explains how a lab that played the long game produced ideas that became the foundation of the modern world.

items.title: The Ideas of Our Constitution (The Seen and the Unseen, Ep 164)
items.creator: Amit Varma
items.why: It lays out the transformative, top-down view of the Indian constitution that Amit argues against here.

items.title: The importance of services exports
items.creator: Ajay Shah
items.why: Shows how telecom made services tradable and why remote work after COVID opened a new phase of globalization for India.

items.title: The Indus Valley Playbook
items.creator: Sajith Pai
items.why: It divides Indians by income into a small affluent top, a middle class with middle-income-country lives, and a large base living like sub-Saharan Africa. Useful for anyone tempted to call India a market of 1.4 billion.

items.title: The industry structure of India's large firms: IT is the biggest industry
items.creator: Ajay Shah
items.why: It supports his one-line summary of the Indian economy (IT and IT-enabled services sold to the West) and his argument that early science and higher-education investments seeded it.

items.title: The Insider
items.creator: PV Narasimha Rao
items.why: Rao's insider's political skill made Manmohan Singh's economics politically possible.

items.title: The Insurgents
items.creator: Fred Kaplan
items.why: It is a recent book that covers Petraeus and later developments in counterinsurgency thinking. It also has the clean summary of Galula's step-by-step method that Amit reads out on the show.

items.title: The investment technology of foreign and domestic institutional investors in an emerging market
items.creator: Ila Patnaik and Ajay Shah
items.why: Looks at foreign equity capital, one of the modes of internationalisation discussed in the episode.

items.title: The iPhone Thought Experiment
items.creator: Tim Urban
items.why: Shows how much of what we know depends on a material and social web that no single person, or even all of humanity, could quickly rebuild.

items.title: The Ivory Throne
items.creator: Manu Pillai
items.why: Documents that it was once common for women in Kerala to be bare-breasted, before British prudery changed things.

items.title: The Jackson Katz quote on passive sentence constructions
items.creator: Jackson Katz
items.why: It shows how the passive voice ('how many women were raped' rather than 'how many men raped women') takes the focus off the men committing violence.

items.title: The Julia Programming Language
items.creator: Viral Shah (co-creator)
items.why: Ajay calls it one of the great achievements of modern programming. It lets you write clean, understandable code at the frontier of performance, and he thinks it is transformative for statistics and data science.

items.title: The Knowledge Project Podcast
items.creator: Shane Parrish
items.why: Amit calls it 'the excellent Knowledge Project podcast'.

items.title: The Köln Concert
items.creator: Keith Jarrett
items.why: A celebrated masterpiece improvised on a substandard piano Jarrett had never played. It is the best illustration of creativity coming from mess.

items.title: The Lady Tasting Tea
items.creator: David Salsburg
items.why: Fun even if you have never studied statistics. It shows how simple questions led to the concepts and mathematics of testing and blind testing.

items.title: The Language Instinct
items.creator: Steven Pinker
items.why: He calls it a great book on how the structures of language are built into the brain. Even so, a child who never hears words won't speak.

items.title: The Lanterne Rouge Cycling Podcast
items.creator: Patrick and Benji
items.why: Hour-long deep dives after races and great previews from two young, deeply involved enthusiasts. Amit says they add a different dimension from Chris Horner.

items.title: The Last Waltz
items.creator: Martin Scorsese
items.why: In the late 1970s The Band, often Dylan's backing band on tour, decided to retire after one last concert and invited friends to perform, including Dylan and Van Morrison (Amit's favourite). Scorsese filmed it. Amit calls it 'absolutely stirring stuff'.

items.title: The Libertarian Mind: A Manifesto for Freedom
items.creator: David Boaz
items.why: Boaz is one of Amit's modern heroes, a great thinker who died recently. The book is a clear statement of the case for freedom.

items.title: The Libertarian Reader
items.creator: David Boaz
items.why: It collects essays by liberal thinkers such as Milton Friedman and Friedrich Hayek, a good distillation of many strands of thought. Amit asks readers not to be put off by the label in the title.

items.title: The Life and Music of Shubha Mudgal (The Seen and the Unseen, Ep 426)
items.creator: Amit Varma with Shubha Mudgal
items.why: 'My great episode with her', in which Mudgal reveals revisionist history and attempts to rename ragas in Hindustani classical music.

items.title: The Life and Times of Abhinandan Sekhri (The Seen and the Unseen, Ep 254)
items.creator: Amit Varma with Abhinandan Sekhri
items.why: The listener felt he was sitting in a living room with two friends, so much so that he interrupted them.

items.title: The Life and Times of Ira Pande (The Seen and the Unseen, Ep 369)
items.creator: Amit Varma
items.why: Another first-hand view of Shivani and her family.

items.title: The Life and Times of Nilanjana Roy (The Seen and the Unseen, Ep 284)
items.creator: Amit Varma with Nilanjana Roy
items.why: Over 5 hours 45 minutes it leaned heavily on ideas and never reached her years in journalism. It still became a sleeper hit in his top ten by downloads, which shows his structural rules are guides rather than laws.

items.title: The Life and Times of Shanta Gokhale (The Seen and the Unseen, Ep 311)
items.creator: Amit Varma with Shanta Gokhale
items.why: An eighty-three-year-old woman of many parts, given roughly one hour per decade of her life. Even Jerry Pinto points listeners to it.

items.title: The Life and Work of Ashwini Deshpande (The Seen and the Unseen, Ep 298)
items.creator: Amit Varma with Ashwini Deshpande
items.why: An economist's view of the puzzle of women's labour-force participation in India.

items.title: The Light Has Gone Out of Our Lives
items.creator: Jawaharlal Nehru
items.why: He says that raspy voice still does something to you across all these years.

items.title: The Logic of Life
items.creator: Tim Harford
items.why: Popular economics that shows how economic reasoning explains everyday life. Once you absorb such fundamentals, everything else starts to make sense.

items.title: The Loneliness of the Long-Distance Runner
items.creator: Alan Sillitoe
items.why: He calls it Sillitoe's 'great novel'. It is the inspiration behind his series of episode titles.

items.title: The Loneliness of the Long-Distance Trucker (The Seen and the Unseen, Ep 192)
items.creator: Amit Varma with Rajat Ubhaykar
items.why: It is a conversation with Rajat Ubhaykar, who wrote a book about trucking across India.

items.title: The Long Divergence
items.creator: Timur Kuran
items.why: It knocks down the usual explanations for the Middle East's economic stagnation and shows how inheritance law and the waqf held it back. Amit says it is worth reading even if you have no interest in Islam or the Middle East, because it shows how incentives shape societies.

items.title: The Looking-Glass Self
items.why: It frames the question of who we are once there is no one left to reflect us back.

items.title: The Machinery of Freedom
items.creator: David Friedman
items.why: Amit calls it a magnificent and very libertarian book. He was delighted that Ajay, whom he teases as a 'secret statist', cited it.

items.title: The Mahabharata
items.why: Amit calls it 'such a masterpiece'. Read as a product of its times, it has every great storytelling trope, and he argues it survives because of magnificent storytelling and not only its religious status.

items.title: The Making of the Atomic Bomb
items.creator: Richard Rhodes
items.why: It explains the science while carrying a lay reader along. Ajay says even people who think they aren't science-literate should read it, because all great acts of creation are human projects. In his preface, Rhodes describes the early-20th-century physics community adopting him as their poet laureate.

items.title: The Man of System (excerpted from The Theory of Moral Sentiments)
items.creator: Adam Smith
items.why: It is the classic statement of the arrogance of imagining society as pieces on a chessboard that a planner can move at will.

items.title: The Man-eating Leopard of Rudraprayag
items.creator: Jim Corbett
items.why: One of the three Corbett books he considers great.

items.title: The Market for 'Lemons'
items.creator: George Akerlof
items.why: Akerlof showed that when buyers can't judge quality, prices fall. A platform that watches workers closely removes that information gap, so the logic says such monitoring should push workers' pay up, not down.

items.title: The Martian
items.creator: Ridley Scott
items.why: It is a vivid yardstick for what a state 'make' organisation can achieve. Ajay adds that bragging rights alone don't create spillovers.

items.title: The match fixing suggestion (X post)
items.why: The viral footage behind Amit's charge that it amounted to a kind of match fixing.

items.title: The Mating Mind
items.creator: Geoffrey Miller
items.why: Part of the group of books that showed him how biology works on human desire, and on his reading list for this subject.

items.title: The Medical Council of India (The Seen and the Unseen, Ep 8)
items.creator: Amit Varma with Pavan Srinath
items.why: It looks at the regulator side of the supply shortage that drives the craziness of medical entrance exams.

items.title: The Memoirs of Dr Haimabati Sen
items.creator: Geraldine Forbes and Tapan Raychaudhuri (editors)
items.why: It tells, in her own words, how a destitute child widow became a doctor. It is now available in print and on Kindle.

items.title: The Minimalists and The Minimalism Game
items.creator: Joshua Fields Millburn
items.why: Millburn's idea that a happy life comes from subtracting, not adding. The game is a 30-day pact where you give away one item on day one, two on day two, and so on, and it reportedly gets tough in week two.

items.title: The Missionary Position: Mother Teresa in Theory and Practice
items.creator: Christopher Hitchens
items.why: It is about Mother Teresa and why one should always be suspicious of sanctimony. Amit wants people to read it and make up their own minds. He calls Hitchens a great writer who died too young and who called out the bullshit on both left and right.

items.title: The Network is the Computer
items.creator: Bradford Morgan White
items.why: Further reading on the company whose leap into CPUs opens the episode.

items.title: The New Face of Cricket
items.creator: Amit Varma
items.why: For readers who want more of his argument that the game's grammar had changed while most teams hadn't noticed.

items.title: The New World Upon Us
items.creator: Amit Varma
items.why: His fuller account of why AlphaZero's self-taught chess was a turning point.

items.title: The Nurture Assumption: Why Children Turn Out the Way They Do
items.creator: Judith Rich Harris
items.why: Amit calls it one of the seminal social science books of the last century. It argues that peers, not parents, have the biggest influence on how children turn out, which is why the neighbourhood and school matter so much.

items.title: The O-Ring Model (Marginal Revolution University video)
items.creator: Tyler Cowen
items.why: He calls it fantastic and says it explains the model in detail, better than his own on-air summary.

items.title: The O-Ring Theory of Economic Development
items.creator: Michael Kremer
items.why: It explains with simple multiplication why small differences in skill create huge differences in output and pay, and why the best people cluster together.

items.title: The Obesity Code
items.creator: Jason Fung
items.why: Part of the core reading that convinced Amit that the standard dietary wisdom on weight is wrong.

items.title: The Odd Woman and the City
items.creator: Vivian Gornick
items.why: He fell in love with Gornick's writing and says it made him want to write. He gifted the book to Nomsita, they have been reading paragraphs aloud to each other on this trip, and he got Ajay to read a couple of pages too. He calls it a desert island book and 'the best kind of writing which just makes your brain explode'.

items.title: The Open Society and Its Enemies
items.creator: Karl Popper
items.why: Source of Popper's diagnosis that nationalism appeals to tribal instinct and lets people escape the strain of individual responsibility.

items.title: The original GST report from 2004
items.creator: Vijay Kelkar, Arbind Modi and Ajay Shah
items.why: It is the origin of India's GST. Ajay says the right fix today is exactly what it proposed: a single low rate, a comprehensive base and no blockage of input tax credit.

items.title: The Origins of Political Order
items.creator: Francis Fukuyama
items.why: He calls the two volumes magisterial. Over a long sweep of history they show how the state evolved, which you need in order to understand the interplay between state and society.

items.title: The Origins of Totalitarianism
items.creator: Hannah Arendt
items.why: Arendt was among the first to show how much Nazi Germany and Stalin's Russia had in common, which makes her an essential guide to authoritarian regimes. Amit adds that it is not a book of history but 'a book of the present moment.'

items.title: The Outsider (L'Etranger)
items.creator: Albert Camus
items.why: A Camus novel Amit has read and remembers well enough to quote.

items.title: The Outsiders
items.creator: Francis Ford Coppola
items.why: Worth knowing as the companion piece to Rumblefish. Amit does not praise it separately.

items.title: The Paperclip Maximizer
items.why: An explainer of the scenario in which a machine built to maximise paperclips turns everything into paperclips.

items.title: The Parable of the Pottery Class
items.creator: Ali Abdaal
items.why: A short telling of the experiment where the group that made many pots beat the group that planned one perfect pot.

items.title: The Paris Review Book for Planes, Trains, Elevators, and Waiting Rooms
items.creator: The Paris Review
items.why: Its stories run from elevator-ride length to long-haul-flight length. That makes it ideal when you want fiction but not a novel's full immersion.

items.title: The Party: The Secret World of China's Communist Rulers
items.creator: Richard McGregor
items.why: He calls it a great book on how the party really works. It shows the Leninist machinery under China's reforms: control of personnel, propaganda and the army, a party above the law, the red phone, and the 'take it or leave it' compact.

items.title: The perfect treatment for diabetes and weight loss (Jason Fung interviewed by Diet Doctor)
items.creator: Jason Fung
items.why: It explains why frequent eating means frequent insulin spikes and moves you toward insulin resistance.

items.title: The Peter Cat Recording Company
items.why: The band has a cult following that forms its own community. Amit tells Ajay 'we will introduce you to some good music.'

items.title: The Plague
items.creator: Albert Camus
items.why: Camus's novel of an epidemic, offered as a natural companion to a conversation about disease and imagination.

items.title: The Pleasures of Reading in an Age of Distraction
items.creator: Alan Jacobs
items.why: A contemporary take on reading well amid the distractions this episode keeps fighting.

items.title: The Poetic Feminism of Paromita Vohra (The Seen and the Unseen, Ep 339)
items.creator: Amit Varma with Paromita Vohra
items.why: Paromita Vohra makes the same point from a very different field: organisations everywhere optimise for the mean and shut out people who think differently.

items.title: The poetry of Mark Strand
items.creator: Mark Strand
items.why: The other poet he would teach instead.

items.title: The poetry of Mary Oliver
items.creator: Mary Oliver
items.why: What schools should be teaching instead of the Romantic poets.

items.title: The policy questions around airlines
items.creator: Ajay Shah
items.why: It is a deep dive into a single industry. He uses it to raise the episode's opening question: is it better to work through one practical case at a time or to learn the general principles in their own right?

items.title: The Population Bomb
items.creator: Paul Ehrlich
items.why: A case study in confident doom. It declared the battle to feed humanity already lost and predicted hundreds of millions would starve in the 1970s and 80s, which never happened.

items.title: The Poverty of Development Economics
items.creator: Deepak Lal
items.why: Further reading for anyone who wants to dig into the episode's main theme of where development economics went astray. It is not discussed in the conversation itself.

items.title: The Power of the Powerless
items.creator: Václav Havel
items.why: He calls it a wonderful extended essay and notes the latest edition has an introduction by Timothy Snyder, also worth reading.

items.title: The Prado, Reina Sofía and Thyssen museums, Madrid
items.why: They cover different eras: the Prado runs from the Renaissance to Goya, the Reina Sofía has modern art and lots of Picasso, and the Thyssen covers much of the 20th century, including pop art. With context, together they amount to a full education in art.

items.title: The Prem Panicker Files (The Seen and the Unseen, Ep 217)
items.creator: Amit Varma
items.why: More of Prem's first-hand experience of how Indian media changed, from the man Amit calls a legend.

items.title: The Price of Onions
items.creator: Ashok Desai
items.why: Tomatoes swinging between Rs 200 and Rs 2 a kg is the same story the book tells, with tomatoes in place of onions. India has been through this before.

items.title: The Problem (Washington Post on the Melitopol counteroffensive)
items.creator: The Washington Post
items.why: Background on the challenge of Ukraine's push toward Melitopol and the Sea of Azov.

items.title: The Problem of Political Authority
items.creator: Michael Huemer
items.why: Amit says it is a book entirely about state legitimacy and that listeners should also read it.

items.title: The problems in India's official data (Episode 21 of Big Ideas)
items.creator: Big Ideas, featuring Rajeshwari Sengupta
items.why: He credits Sengupta with being 'clever and insightful' in understanding the difficulties in India's GDP measurement and telling those stories well.

items.title: The Procrastination Matrix
items.creator: Tim Urban
items.why: Urban writes about exactly Amit's dilemma: living in the urgent or the trivial quadrants and never reaching the important-but-not-urgent one.

items.title: The Project Oasis Report
items.creator: Project Oasis expert committee, led by Surendra Dave
items.why: It is the founding document of Indian pension reform: defined contributions, individual accounts and cheap index funds.

items.title: The Promise (version on 18 Tracks)
items.creator: Bruce Springsteen
items.why: Ajay sees Born to Run, Thunder Road and The Promise as a triad: 'three windows into the same people, into the same life'. He prefers the version on 18 Tracks.

items.title: The quest for economic freedom in India
items.creator: Shruti Rajagopalan
items.why: He calls it 'absolutely magisterial'. It catalogues the nationalisations, 350% tariffs, 97.75% income tax and the scarcity-era jokes of that period.

items.title: The Question That Steve Jobs Used to Ask Jony Ive Every Day
items.why: Source of the lesson to 'learn to say no to things that you love', which is the real discipline of focus.

items.title: The Reason British Kit Kats Taste Better Than America's
items.creator: Gregory Lovvorn
items.why: Background on why the British Kit Kat that fans revere differs from the American one.

items.title: The Reflections of Samarth Bansal (The Seen and the Unseen, Ep 299)
items.creator: Amit Varma
items.why: Samarth is the source of the ideas of 'civic purpose', 'invisible quitting', and India's 'shallow ecosystem' of media experiments.

items.title: The Right to Property (The Seen and the Unseen, Ep 26)
items.creator: Amit Varma with Shruti Rajagopalan
items.why: Rajagopalan explains at length what this restriction leads to: depressed land prices, land-use-change scams, and farmers who can't exit agriculture.

items.title: The Rise of the Creative Class
items.creator: Richard Florida
items.why: It argues that growth follows creative congregation: open, diverse cities draw entrepreneurs, artists and gay and lesbian communities, and capital then chases that talent.

items.title: The Rising Price of Husbands
items.creator: Vijayendra Rao
items.why: One of Amit's favourite titles: clever and also accurately about the paper.

items.title: The River
items.creator: Bruce Springsteen
items.why: Amit calls it a great song whose opening section is brilliant. It shows Springsteen turning his family's ordinary life into a story with its own momentum.

items.title: The RODE Wireless PRO is NUTS!
items.creator: DLSR Video Shooter
items.why: A hands-on review of the gear behind the hosts' new 'level of human freedom'.

items.title: The Romantic Recession report
items.why: It documents falling trust among singles: women avoiding dating strangers, and men feeling women don't give them a fair chance.

items.title: The science fiction of Margaret Atwood, Ursula Le Guin, Ted Chiang and Ken Liu
items.creator: Margaret Atwood, Ursula Le Guin, Ted Chiang, Ken Liu
items.why: People dismiss science fiction as genre entertainment. Amit thinks the best of it deals with the biggest questions of our time, and that reading it is really a way of thinking about the present.

items.title: The Second Bakery Attack
items.creator: Haruki Murakami
items.why: The example Amit names of the high-quality fiction Playboy carried.

items.title: The Second World Wars
items.creator: Victor Davis Hanson
items.why: It is very hard to write a genuinely new book on WWII, and Ajay says Hanson has done it, with deeper ideas, a more meta-level analysis and implications for today's world.

items.title: The secret world beneath our feet is mind-blowing – and the key to our planet's future
items.creator: George Monbiot
items.why: Background reading on the soil life that Ajay argues makes soil-grown food nutritionally superior.

items.title: The Seen and the Unseen episode on GST with Devangshu Datta (January 2017)
items.creator: Amit Varma
items.why: Devangshu correctly predicted everything that would go wrong with the GST.

items.title: The Seen and the Unseen episode on GST with Shruti Rajagopalan (June 2018)
items.creator: Amit Varma
items.why: Amit describes it as a comprehensive treatment of the GST.

items.title: The Seen and the Unseen episode with Arnold Kling
items.creator: Amit Varma
items.why: An audio companion to the book. Here Kling adds a fourth tribe, Trumpism/MAGA, to his original three.

items.title: The Seen and the Unseen episode with Jerry Rao on Indian conservatism
items.creator: Amit Varma
items.why: A lively disagreement in which Amit argues that Burkean conservatism barely exists in India. He recommends it to anyone who thinks he never argues with his guests.

items.title: The Semiconductor Wars (The Seen and the Unseen, Ep 358)
items.creator: Amit Varma with Pranay Kotasthane and Abhiram Manchi
items.why: It is a long-form deep dive on chips to accompany the book recommendations.

items.title: The Seven Basic Plots
items.creator: Christopher Booker
items.why: Amit calls it excellent. It explains why Beowulf, Jaws, James Bond and Sholay are the same story underneath, and he presents it as a lens for writers rather than a rulebook.

items.title: The Seven Basic Plots (Everything is Everything, Ep 69)
items.creator: Amit Varma and Ajay Shah
items.why: Makes the point that a constraint doesn't stop great work. The Beatles and the Stones did brilliant things inside fixed formats.

items.title: The Shallows
items.creator: Nicholas Carr
items.why: A rare essay-turned-book that earns its length. It develops the case that the form of our engagement, phone or book, shapes how deeply we think.

items.title: The Shock of the New
items.creator: Robert Hughes
items.why: Amit calls it a masterpiece too.

items.title: The Simon–Ehrlich wager
items.why: Background on the 1980 wager in which all five metals Ehrlich chose (copper, chromium, nickel, tin and tungsten) were cheaper by 1990.

items.title: The social and economic roots of Newton's Principia
items.creator: Boris Hessen
items.why: It challenged the great man theory by tracing Newton to English conditions: freedom, sea power, tinkering. Its boldest move was linking capitalism to the world of ideas, which Ajay thinks was ahead of its time.

items.title: The Solution
items.creator: Bertolt Brecht
items.why: In a few lines it skewers a state that blames its people instead of serving them.

items.title: The Spirit of Indian Painting
items.creator: BN Goswamy
items.why: It does for Indian art what Gombrich does for art in general. A classic and a masterpiece.

items.title: The Sporting Spirit
items.creator: George Orwell
items.why: The 'great essay' that called sport 'war minus the shooting', drawing on an ugly football match involving a Moscow team and a riot in Spain. It frames the India-Pakistan cricket episode.

items.title: The State of the Media (The Seen and the Unseen, Ep 46)
items.creator: Amit Varma
items.why: Amit says Prem's episodes with him are really good. Prem is a legend in the field and the source of insights like the Yahoo story and 'a mile wide and an inch deep'.

items.title: The Story of My Experiments with Truth
items.creator: Mohandas Gandhi
items.why: It shows in great detail how Gandhi was 'quite a weirdo', a reminder of how unconventional great free thinkers look up close.

items.title: The strategy and the tactics
items.creator: Ajay Shah
items.why: Ajay's own writing on a theme of the episode: government needs overall strategic thinking rather than a rush to act.

items.title: The Struggle and the Promise
items.creator: Naushad Forbes
items.why: Written by a business leader who backed reform publicly when few others did.

items.title: The Sun Also Rises
items.creator: Ernest Hemingway
items.why: Its exchange on going bankrupt, 'slowly at first and then suddenly', is the classic description of how distress plays out.

items.title: The Surface Area of Serendipity (Everything is Everything, Ep 39)
items.creator: Amit Varma and Ajay Shah
items.why: It's the fuller case for persistence and bias for action as the way to give luck more chances to find you.

items.title: The Takshashila Institution
items.why: Its weekly ritual of researchers presenting what they learned that week is Amit's living example of multidisciplinary group learning. He says it leaves your brain cells all fired up.

items.title: The tech wars are about to enter a fiery new phase
items.creator: The Economist
items.why: It argues, correctly in Amit's view, that these tech and trade wars are bad for the US, bad for China and bad for the rest of the world.

items.title: The Tell-Tale Brain
items.creator: VS Ramachandran
items.why: It explains the science behind empathy: mirror neurons copy the experiences of others when we hear about them. That is part of why reading other people's lives works on us.

items.title: The Tesseract
items.creator: Alex Garland
items.why: The Beach is Garland's more famous novel, but Amit prefers The Tesseract and calls it fantastic.

items.title: The Theory of Economic Regulation
items.creator: George Stigler
items.why: A famous 1971 essay with three axioms. The state has coercive power; private parties benefit from steering it; so every private party has a rational self-interest in trying to. It explains why lobbying is inevitable and why you must be super careful.

items.title: The Third Way
items.creator: Rahul Matthan
items.why: Its discussion of credit decisions tailored to individuals with big data.

items.title: The Tibet Museum, McLeod Ganj
items.why: Unlike many Indian museums it is done well, with artefacts that trigger the mind. Walking the lanes of a living government in exile also makes you think hard about what a state is.

items.title: The Time a Stiff Caught Fire
items.creator: Keith Yates
items.why: It tells the full story of the fan who got 'Piano Man' onto the radio and saved Billy Joel's career, which shows how much luck decides what we later call great art.

items.title: The Tipping Point
items.creator: Malcolm Gladwell
items.why: It helps you ask whether you are a deep specialist or someone who links people, and whether you should deliberately stretch toward the other.

items.title: The Truth About Ourselves
items.creator: Amit Varma
items.why: Many of the findings Amit reads out in the episode are quoted from this essay.

items.title: The tweet that inspired this episode
items.creator: @NoContextHumans
items.why: The question that set off the whole episode about lost objects.

items.title: The Tyranny of Experts
items.creator: William Easterly
items.why: Recommended alongside Easterly's other books as essential reading for understanding how the world of development really works.

items.title: The U.S. Finally Has a Strategy to Compete With China. Will It Work?
items.creator: Greg Ip
items.why: Amit calls it a wonderful piece that lays out the what and how of the shift, from a bipartisan pro-trade, engage-China consensus to a new bipartisan consensus that America is at war with China.

items.title: The Ultimate Resource
items.creator: Julian Simon
items.why: Its thesis that human beings are the ultimate resource is the root of the 'people are brains, not stomachs' worldview.

items.title: The ULTIMATE Tour de France 2024 Preview
items.creator: Lanterne Rouge Cycling Podcast
items.why: A ready-made primer before watching the 2024 Tour, which started the weekend this episode was released.

items.title: The US Government order accepting its mistake on Oppenheimer
items.why: It is the primary document of a state formally admitting its error, which Ajay holds up as what a first-world state looks like.

items.title: The Velvet Underground
items.creator: The Velvet Underground
items.why: The band is a model for James C Scott: little known to the public, but hugely influential on the people who go on to influence everyone else.

items.title: The Vision of the Anointed: Self-Congratulation as a Basis for Social Policy
items.creator: Thomas Sowell
items.why: A great book whose subtitle sums up the episode. It shows that elites treating disagreement as sin rather than error is at least 200 years old.

items.title: The War Against Cliche
items.creator: Martin Amis
items.why: A great collection of Amis's criticism. It is built around the fact that cliché is what writers most fear, which shows how much of human expression is autopilot.

items.title: The White Crow Books and Coffee
items.why: Ajay calls it Bombay's great new tourist attraction. Its strength is curation rather than size, and both hosts have bought books there.

items.title: The Wind
items.creator: Warren Zevon
items.why: Amit calls it a great album. Zevon made it after a terminal diagnosis, knowing he would die, surrounded by friends who played with him.

items.title: The Winning Mantra for this IPL: Attack, Attack, Attack
items.creator: Amit Varma
items.why: Another instalment of his argument that the EV of aggression in T20 is far higher than teams assume.

items.title: The Wizard and the Prophet
items.creator: Charles C Mann
items.why: It covers the tension between the scientific and industrial revolution in agriculture and concerns about sustainability. Ajay calls this the great food-system question of the next 25 years: how to feed 1.4 billion people sustainably, in a way that also fits with public health.

items.title: The Wonders of FDI (Everything is Everything, Ep 111)
items.creator: Amit Varma and Ajay Shah
items.why: Fair treatment of foreign firms, including protection against expropriation, is part of deep integration.

items.title: The World of Yesterday
items.creator: Stefan Zweig
items.why: Zweig's memoir of living through Europe's collapse into fascism, Bolshevism and nationalism. Amit reads out its 'pale horses of the apocalypse' passage.

items.title: The WRONG Way to Fight Extremists (Everything is Everything, Ep 4)
items.creator: Amit Varma and Ajay Shah
items.why: It is where they cover insurgencies and counterinsurgency, which this episode deliberately skips.

items.title: The WSJ story on Trump
items.creator: The Wall Street Journal
items.why: Ajay uses it as an example of journalism you can trust: a paper wouldn't take on someone famous for suing without doing the hard work.

items.title: Thelma and Louise
items.creator: Ridley Scott
items.why: It is one of his favourite films of all time. It comes with a story he says 'should be true' even if it isn't: Saudi censors cut every shot of women driving, leaving a four-minute film.

items.title: There be dragons: Off-balance-sheet liabilities of the Indian State
items.creator: Ila Patnaik and Ajay Shah
items.why: Companion reading to Ajay's warning that the UPS guarantee may become a contingent liability hanging over the Indian state.

items.title: They Stole a Bridge. They Stole a Pond
items.creator: Amit Varma
items.why: Amit's own piece on the thefts he uses to illustrate India's raw, misdirected ingenuity.

items.title: Thinking Strategically: The Competitive Edge in Business, Politics, and Everyday Life
items.creator: Avinash Dixit and Barry Nalebuff
items.why: Draws on game theory ('strategically' in the sense of John von Neumann) and brings that body of knowledge close to real-world applications. Ajay thinks anyone grappling with reality will benefit from it.

items.title: This century and the last one: A report card for the first 10 years
items.creator: Ajay Shah
items.why: Ajay's own long-horizon look at how the century was going. It is context for his calm about technological disruption.

items.title: This is Water
items.creator: David Foster Wallace
items.why: Its parable, where a fish asks 'what's water?', captures how the things we normalise become invisible. That is the lens Amit uses to examine electricity.

items.title: This miracle plant was eaten into extinction 2,000 years ago -- or was it?
items.creator: Taras Grescoe
items.why: The full story of the lost Roman herb and the possible modern rediscovery that Ajay is waiting for 'with bated breath'.

items.title: Thomas Frank's YouTube channel
items.creator: Thomas Frank
items.why: Another creator who started small and built himself up by practising what he teaches. Good for working out which tools and ways of thinking suit you.

items.title: Thomas Sowell interviewed by Peter Robinson
items.creator: Peter Robinson with Thomas Sowell
items.why: Sowell, who wrote about Smoot-Hawley decades ago, says today's tariffs are the same thing happening again.

items.title: Three holes in the U.S.' economic strategy against China
items.creator: Noah Smith
items.why: It makes the point Amit wants: instead of export restrictions, America could deregulate its own industry so more people build drones at home. This is his model for answering cheap Chinese imports through domestic freedom rather than bans.

items.title: Three page notes considered harmful
items.creator: Ajay Shah
items.why: It describes the pathology: a half-baked idea, a three-page note, three practitioners consulted, no thinkers at the table, and then a bad idea gets implemented.

items.title: Tiago Forte on productivity
items.creator: Tiago Forte
items.why: A corrective to treating productivity as nothing but ticking off tasks.

items.title: Tiffany Ryder's tweet on insecure doctors
items.creator: Tiffany Ryder
items.why: Her retort, that any doctor threatened by WebMD should have studied harder, raises the question of what expertise means when information is a click away.

items.title: Tim Urban on The Lex Fridman Podcast
items.creator: Lex Fridman
items.why: Amit loved how Urban built up to it. He began with the fact that no one can make a pencil, then took apart Fridman's assumption that a thousand people with metals could build an iPhone.

items.title: Tim Urban's tweet on getting to know people
items.creator: Tim Urban
items.why: 'Whenever I get to know someone who seems perfect, I end up disappointed. Whenever I get to know someone who I think is the worst of the worst, I'm pleasantly surprised. Angels and demons aren't real.' It is a reminder to judge people less and stay open to them.

items.title: Time
items.creator: Pink Floyd
items.why: The line 'plans that either come to naught or half a page of scribbled lines' sums up his Zen attitude towards abandoned work.

items.title: To GST or not to GST
items.creator: Vijay Kelkar, Arbind Modi and Ajay Shah
items.why: Amit calls it brilliant and incredibly insightful. It sets out the many ways the GST can still be improved, and Ajay leans on its legal analysis of how input tax credit has been blocked as the starting point for any fix.

items.title: To Have or To Be?
items.creator: Erich Fromm
items.why: Fromm's 1976 book was a pioneer on these questions: how to move beyond the simple consumerism many Indians discovered only in the last 20–30 years, towards a better sense of why we are here and what gives life meaning.

items.title: To the Castle and Back
items.creator: Václav Havel
items.why: Amit calls it a wonderful book.

items.title: Toba Tek Singh
items.creator: Saadat Hasan Manto
items.why: Amit calls it a great short story about one of the most tragic borders, and one that is close to home.

items.title: Toddy Chicken recipe video
items.creator: Wah Chef
items.why: His personal favourite in the flood of online cooking videos.

items.title: Too Many People?
items.creator: Nicholas Eberstadt
items.why: It finds no correlation between population density and poverty, with striking counterexamples: Monaco is forty times as dense as Bangladesh and far richer, and Bahrain is three times as dense as India and far richer.

items.title: Top500.org
items.why: Of the 500 most powerful computers in the world, roughly 490 or more run some variant of Unix.

items.title: Tour de France (Wikipedia)
items.why: A primer for anyone who wants to start watching the Tour.

items.title: Towards Estimating India's Implicit Pension Debt
items.creator: Gautam Bhardwaj and Surendra Dave
